title: Chelsea part ways with head of women’s football Paul Green
author: Cerys Jones
content:
Chelsea have parted ways with head of women’s football Paul Green.

Green first joined Chelsea in February 2013 as part of Emma Hayes’ coaching staff, moving from fellow Women’s Super League (WSL) side Doncaster Rovers Belles to become Hayes’ assistant manager.

In his 13 years with Chelsea, Green earned recognition inside and outside the club as being one of the most important figures in the evolution of Chelsea into the modern-day domestic behemoth it is.

As general manager, Green was tasked with player recruitment, helping to build one of English women’s football’s most impressive squads. Alongside Hayes, Green played an integral role in building a culture of winning and many around the game recognised Green as the unsung architect to Chelsea’s success.

Green was a central figure in appointing Sonia Bompastor as Hayes’ successor in 2024, working with the club’s co-sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Laurence Stewart.

Green’s departure comes after Chelsea announced a two-year contract extension for Bompastor, who has faced scrutiny after Chelsea suffered successive league defeats for the first time since 2015, courtesy of defeats to Arsenal and Manchester City.

Despite Bompastor leading Chelsea to a sixth-successive WSL title last season with an unbeaten record, the French coach’s second season in charge has been less convincing with Chelsea struggling to display their usual infallibility.

By Football Writer Cerys Jones

Paul Green might not be a well-known name to the general public, preferring to operate out of the limelight, but those of Chelsea affiliation will know that this departure is likely to signify a mighty transition of the women’s team.

Green’s role is nominally ‘head of women’s football’ and includes a heavy influence on recruitment. They are masters of succession planning and Green should be credited with their slick operations over the years.

His work in tandem with Hayes is seen as critical to Chelsea’s growth into the WSL’s dominant force.

At a time when, after damaging consecutive defeats, Chelsea attempted to restore stability with a contract extension for head coach Sonia Bompastor, this news only adds to the noise around the club once more.
